query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Using machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) trained on ab initio liquid-state configurations as reference models for thermodynamic integration in multicomponent high-entropy alloys (HEAs) at and near their melting temperatures will significantly improve reference–target phase-space overlap compared to traditional EAM references, thereby reducing integration path mismatch and free-energy errors.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloy (HEA) in solid and liquid states, near and above melting temperature.
generation.intervention: Replace EAM reference potentials with MLIPs (e.g., neural network or moment tensor potentials) trained on ab initio liquid-state configurations for thermodynamic integration.
generation.conditions: Applicable to HEAs with 4–6 principal elements, at temperatures from just below to above the melting point (e.g., 0.9–1.1 T_m), and compositions where ab initio liquid snapshots can be generated.
generation.structural_mediator: MLIP reference captures diverse atomic environments and short-range order present in ab initio liquid, unlike EAM.
generation.mechanism: MLIPs trained on liquid-state ab initio data encode many-body interactions and local structural diversity, increasing overlap between reference and target phase spaces and reducing the mismatch in thermodynamic integration paths.
generation.predicted_outcome: Thermodynamic integration using MLIP references will yield free energies within 10–20 meV/atom of direct ab initio calculations, representing a substantial reduction (by at least a factor of 2) in path mismatch and error compared to EAM references, which typically show larger discrepancies due to poor liquid-state representation.
generation.baseline: EAM reference potentials, which are known to poorly represent ab initio liquid configurations in multicomponent alloys, leading to significant integration path mismatch and free-energy errors.
generation.boundary: Hypothesis applies to HEAs where MLIP training data can be generated for relevant compositions and temperatures; may not apply to alloys with extreme chemical complexity or where MLIP training is infeasible.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of improvement depends on MLIP quality and training data diversity; some residual mismatch may persist if MLIP fails to capture rare configurations.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform thermodynamic integration from MLIP reference to ab initio target for a representative HEA at melting temperature, and compare free energy results to those obtained using EAM reference and direct ab initio calculations.
measurements: Free energy difference between MLIP reference and ab initio target
Free energy difference between EAM reference and ab initio target
Reference–target phase-space overlap metrics (e.g., configuration similarity, overlap integrals)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If MLIP reference does not reduce free-energy integration path mismatch and error relative to EAM by at least a factor of 2, or if MLIP reference yields free energies >30 meV/atom away from ab initio values, the hypothesis is falsified.
